disclaimer: UAE tax rules changed materially through 2025/2026. From 1 January 2026 the VAT Law amendments (FDL 16/2025), the Tax Procedures Law amendments (FDL 17/2025), and the sweetened drinks tiered excise (Cabinet Decision 197 of 2025) all apply, and a new AML law (FDL 10/2025) has been in force since 14 October 2025. Small Business Relief now covers eligible tax periods ending through 31 December 2029 under Ministerial Decision 131 of 2026. The unified late-payment penalty (Cabinet Decision 129 of 2025) took effect 14 April 2026. Minimum excise prices for specified tobacco and vaping products apply from 1 September 2026 under Cabinet Decision 137 of 2026. From 1 October 2026 the amended VAT Executive Regulation (Cabinet Decision 149 of 2026), FTA Decision 13 of 2026 on supply verification before input tax deduction, FTA Decision 17 of 2026 on input tax for employee expenses, Ministerial Decision 168 of 2026 on ASP accreditation and Ministerial Decision 197 of 2026 amending the e-invoicing rules all apply. The e-invoicing pilot went live on 1 July 2026; businesses with revenue at or above AED 50M must appoint an Accredited Service Provider by 30 October 2026 (Ministerial Resolution 66 of 2026; no extension had been announced as of 20 October 2026) and go live on 1 January 2027. FTA Decision 12 of 2026 sets a 30 November 2026 DMTT registration deadline for fiscal years ending before 30 April 2026, and the first Top-up Tax return for a calendar-2025 first Transition Year is due 30 June 2027 under Cabinet Decision 142 of 2024. Other upcoming dates: 31 October 2026 for retrospective exemption applications by wholly owned government subsidiaries (FTA Decision 15 of 2026) and 31 December 2026 for refund claims on credit balances older than 5 years (FDL 17/2025 transition). The 30 September 2026 deadline for Corporate Tax returns and payment for calendar-year 2025 periods has passed; any return or payment made after it is late. Always verify against the FTA and MoF portals before quoting figures.

qfzp.name: Qualifying Free Zone Person
qfzp.summary: Eligible free zone persons get 0% on Qualifying Income and 9% on the rest. The ordinary AED 375,000 0% band and Small Business Relief do not apply to a QFZP.
qfzp.saas_note: SaaS is not itself a named Qualifying Activity. Qualification depends on the counterparty, excluded activities and any qualifying intellectual-property income; do not assume all SaaS revenue is non-qualifying. QFZPs do not receive the ordinary AED 375,000 band on non-qualifying taxable income.
qfzp.de_minimis: Lower of 5% of revenue or AED 5,000,000

compliance_procedures_2026.summary: A QFZP relying on the Qualifying Activity of distributing goods or materials in or from a Designated Zone must obtain an agreed-upon procedures report (ISRS 4400) from its external auditor or another UAE-licensed independent auditor. The report must show that customers resell or process the goods for sale, and that any goods the QFZP imports into the State enter through a Designated Zone, backed by customer licences or declarations, sales records and customs or shipping documents.

small_business_relief.name: Small Business Relief
small_business_relief.law: Ministerial Decision 73 of 2023, as amended by Ministerial Decision 131 of 2026
small_business_relief.summary: Eligible resident persons with revenue at or below AED 3M may elect Small Business Relief for tax periods beginning on or after 1 June 2023 and ending on or before 31 December 2029.

registration.waiver_announcement: A Cabinet decision in effect from April 2025 (FTA implementation announced 7 May 2025) waives the AED 10,000 late-registration penalty, or credits it back if already paid, where the first Tax Return or annual declaration is filed within 7 months of the end of the first Tax Period or financial year instead of 9. It applies only to the first Tax Period and covers late-registration penalties from 1 June 2023. The FTA reported more than 68,600 beneficiaries by May 2026.

current_cycle.note: The FTA confirmed that all Taxable Persons with a financial year ended 31 December 2025, including Small Business Relief electors, had to file and pay by 30 September 2026. Other year ends follow the 9-month rule.
current_cycle.deadline_status: PASSED. The 30 September 2026 deadline has expired; returns filed or tax paid after it are late, and unpaid tax attracts the unified late-payment penalty (Cabinet Decision 129 of 2025).

transfer_pricing.tp_disclosure_note: Corporate Tax return disclosure form: the Related Parties schedule applies where the aggregate value of Related Party transactions exceeds AED 40 million, and only transaction categories above AED 4 million must be disclosed; the Connected Persons schedule applies where payments or benefits to a Connected Person exceed AED 500,000. Source: FTA Corporate Tax Returns Guide (CTGTXR1, 11 November 2024).
transfer_pricing.local_master_file_note: Ministerial Decision 97 of 2023 requires a master file and local file where the taxable person's revenue in the tax period is AED 200 million or more, or where it is a constituent entity of an MNE group with total consolidated group revenue of AED 3.15 billion or more.

pillar_two_dmtt.name: Domestic Minimum Top-up Tax
pillar_two_dmtt.applies_to: MNE groups with consolidated revenue of EUR 750 million or more in at least two of the four fiscal years immediately preceding the tested fiscal year

registration_status.status: FTA Decision 12 of 2026 (issued 16 July 2026, published 4 August 2026) sets DMTT registration timelines: register within 7 months of the end of the first in-scope fiscal year, but an entity with a fiscal year ending before 30 April 2026 must register on or before 30 November 2026. A Domestic Designated Filing Entity registers on behalf of the domestic group. Ministerial Decision 133 of 2026 separately identifies Pillar Two Information Return filers. Confirm operational filing requirements with the FTA.
registration_status.first_return_note: Confirmed by primary law: Article 8.1 of the Annexure to Cabinet Decision 142 of 2024 requires the Top-up Tax Return no later than 15 months after the end of the Reporting Fiscal Year, or 18 months for the first Transition Year of any Constituent Entity of the MNE Group, and Article 11 requires payment by the return due date. For a group whose first Transition Year is calendar 2025, the return and payment are due 30 June 2027; other year ends follow the same rule.
registration_status.first_return_basis: Cabinet Decision 142 of 2024, Annexure Article 8.1 (filing) and Article 11 (payment)
registration_status.registration_deadline_general: Within 7 months from the end of the first fiscal year in which the entity is in scope
registration_status.registration_deadline_transitional_appli: Entities with a fiscal year ending before 2026-04-30 (for example, calendar-year 2025)
registration_status.deregistration: Apply within 6 months of ceasing to exist or of the end of the fiscal year in which the entity leaves the MNE group; entities ceasing before 30 June 2026 must apply by 31 December 2026. Out-of-scope notifications are due within 6 months of the tested fiscal year end.
registration_status.guide: FTA Top-up Tax Guide on Scope and Registration (TTGREG1), issue date 26 August 2026 on the FTA guides page and announced by the FTA on 7 October 2026. It restates the 30 November 2026 registration deadline for entities whose first in-scope fiscal year ends before 30 April 2026 and the 7-month rule for all other cases, and covers DDFE registration and the choice of Pillar Two Information Return filer. A companion guide on Excluded Entities and Investment Entities (TTGEIE1) carries the same issue date.

information_return.summary: Requires Pillar Two Information Returns for in-scope UAE constituent entities (excluding investment entities), UAE joint ventures and JV subsidiaries, and UAE-created stateless reverse hybrids. A designated local entity may file on behalf of covered entities.
information_return.foreign_filing_relief: Local filing is relieved where a qualifying return is filed by an ultimate parent or designated filing entity in a jurisdiction with a qualifying competent authority agreement effective for the reporting year; the FTA must still be notified of the filing entity identity and location.
information_return.filing_deadline_note: Article 15 of the Annexure to Cabinet Decision 142 of 2024 requires the Pillar Two Information Return and related notifications no later than 15 months after the end of the Reporting Fiscal Year. Article 15 as published does not state the 18-month first-year rule that Article 8.1 gives the Top-up Tax Return; confirm the first-year filing date with the FTA.

commentary_and_guidance.summary: Adopts the OECD 2026 Consolidated Commentary to the GloBE Model Rules, the OECD Central Record of Pillar Two Administrative Guidance and the January 2025 GloBE Information Return for the purposes of Cabinet Decision 142 of 2024.

sports_entities_exemption.summary: Qualifying non-commercial sports entities (international sports entities, sports entities, and supporting ancillary entities) are exempt from corporate tax retroactively from 1 June 2023. Conditions include recognition by the Ministry of Sports or competent authority and exclusive use of income and assets for the entity's objectives; entities must register and apply for the exemption with the FTA and file an annual declaration.

exemption_applications.summary: Exempt-category persons under Article 4(1)(f) to (i) of the Corporate Tax Law (qualifying public benefit entities, qualifying investment funds, pension and social security funds, qualifying wholly owned subsidiaries and Cabinet-designated persons) must register under the FTA Decision 3 of 2024 timelines and then apply for exemption no later than 90 business days after the end of the tax period in which they met the conditions.
special_deadlines: Persons covered by Cabinet Decision 55 of 2025 applying retrospectively: by 2026-12-31.

Persons covered by a Cabinet decision issued on or after 2026-01-01 (for example Cabinet Decision 1 of 2026 on sports entities) applying retrospectively: within 90 business days from the end of the tax period in which the decision was issued.
Qualifying limited partnership juridical persons under Article 5 of Cabinet Decision 34 of 2025, for 2025 tax periods ending on or before 2026-08-31: by 2026-12-31.
Wholly owned subsidiaries of government or government-controlled entities for tax periods ending before 2026-01-01: by 2026-10-31.

fta_service_fees.note: Cabinet Decision 174 of 2025 revised FTA service fees from 1 January 2026: new fees for Unilateral Advance Pricing Agreement applications, and the paid paper Tax Registration Certificate and Warehouse Keeper Registration Certificate replaced by free electronic certificates with QR-code verification.

guides_2026.note: Confirmed on the FTA guides pages (checked 2026-10-20): Corporate Tax Guide on Taxation of Family Foundations (CTGFF1, 10 June 2026), Basic Tax Information Bulletin on Corporate Tax Losses (25 June 2026), Education Sector VAT Guide (VATGED1, 29 June 2026), Top-up Tax guides TTGREG1 (Scope and Registration) and TTGEIE1 (Excluded Entities and Investment Entities) (both 26 August 2026), VAT Public Clarification VATP046 on the VAT Decree-Law amendments (4 September 2026), and the Free Zones and Designated Zones for Tax Purposes guide (TAXP010, 2 October 2026) covering Corporate Tax, VAT and Excise. No FTA guide was published between 2 and 20 October 2026.

changes: Reverse-charge supplies no longer require self-issued tax invoices; the supporting documents set by the Executive Regulation must be kept instead.

Excess recoverable VAT must be refunded or used within 5 years from the end of the tax period in which it arose, or the right lapses (FTA example: a credit from the period ending 31 January 2026 lapses on 31 January 2031). Older balances fall under the Tax Procedures Law transition, which allows refund claims until 31 December 2026.

New Article 54 bis: the FTA rejects input VAT deduction where the supply or supply chain is linked to tax evasion and the recipient knew, and may reject it where the recipient should have known. A recipient that did not verify the supply before deducting is treated as one that should have known (FTA Decision 13 of 2026 sets the verification steps).
The VAT Law statute-of-limitations article (Article 79 bis) was repealed; limitation periods now sit in the Tax Procedures Law.

directives_2026.binding_basis: Article 54 bis of the Tax Procedures Law provides for directives binding on the FTA and taxpayers within scope.

directives.topic: VAT adjustments after a registrant exits a tax group
Conversion of digital currency values into AED
Fees and charges in life insurance and life reinsurance contracts
Valuation of deemed supplies of services

directives_2026.note: The FTA VAT legislation register lists these five directives published in July 2026. Apply each directive using its original text; this inventory does not reproduce detailed transaction treatments.

supply_verification_2026.subject: Measures, procedures and conditions required by taxable persons to verify the validity and integrity of supplies before deducting input tax (Article 54 bis of the VAT Law).
key_requirements: Verify supplier identity: ID and a meeting for natural persons; incorporation records and the authorised representative's ID for legal persons.
Verify the supplier's actual place of business and its fit with the supplier's activities.
Check risk indicators (more than two address or key-staff changes in 12 months, disproportionate transactions) and keep a justified explanation if any apply.
Where supplies from the supplier exceed or are expected to exceed AED 375,000 over 12 months, obtain a UAE bank confirmation of the supplier's account and review public reviews and media.
Assess commercial rationale, payment method (electronic by default; cash only with a documented reason and within legal thresholds), pricing and the supplier's licensed activity.

executive_regulation_amendments_2026.deferred_provisions: The revised input tax apportionment rules apply from the first tax year commencing after 1 October 2027.
changes: Updated supply and import rules for medical products to match the current healthcare legislative framework.
Clarified input tax recovery on employee accommodation.
Aligned the Capital Assets Scheme scope with the VAT Law.
Refined the input tax apportionment method (existing rules retained for government entities and charities).
New provisions on single composite supplies based on economic substance.
Input tax is not recoverable where consideration above a threshold set by a Minister of Finance decision is paid in cash.
executive_regulation_amendments_2026.cash_threshold_note: The cash-payment threshold is to be prescribed by a separate Minister of Finance decision. No such decision appeared on the MoF or FTA legislation registers as of 2026-10-20, so no figure is asserted here.

employee_expenses_input_tax_2026.summary: Sets the cases and conditions for recovering input tax on goods or services provided free to employees under a contractual obligation or documented policy: transport between home and work or for job duties, food in remote locations without facilities, work-required accommodation, temporary accommodation of up to 30 days for new employees, work phones and data under a documented and monitored policy, and business parking fees. In each case the employee must not be able to take a cash alternative where the decision so requires.

tax_procedures.name: Tax Procedures Law amendments
tax_procedures.law: Federal Decree-Law 17 of 2025 (amending Federal Decree-Law 28 of 2022)

audit_window.summary: The standard 5-year audit and assessment window is extendable up to 15 years for tax evasion or failure to register, and the FTA gets 4 extra years to complete an audit notified before the window expires.

refunds_and_credit_balances.basis: Refunds and credit balances are claimable for a maximum of 5 years from the end of the relevant tax period.
refunds_and_credit_balances.transition: Credit balances whose 5-year period expired before 1 January 2026, or expires within one year of that date, can still be claimed until 31 December 2026 under a 1-year transition; a related voluntary disclosure may follow within 2 years of the claim if the FTA has not yet decided it.

tax_procedures.excise_statute_of_limitations: Consolidated into the Tax Procedures Law; the Excise Tax Law's standalone limitation article was repealed by FDL 17/2025.

esr.name: Economic Substance Regulations
esr.status: DEAD for financial years ending after 2022-12-31
esr.applies_to_periods: Financial years commencing on or after 2019-01-01 and ENDING on or before 2022-12-31. Scope is set by the financial year END date, so a year running into 2023 is already out of scope.
esr.historical_obligations: NOT waived. Cabinet Decision 98 of 2024 cancelled only the requirement to file notifications and reports for financial years ending after 2022-12-31. For in-scope years (2019 to 2022) companies remain liable to file, to answer information and amendment requests from the FTA or the regulatory authority, and to pay any penalties already imposed. The cancellation does not refund penalties for in-scope years.
esr.warning: Do NOT promise ESR filing tools for current periods. The 9 Relevant Activities only matter for historical filings. Do not tell a user that historical ESR penalties are refundable, because the cancellation does not refund them.

key_changes: Fines for legal persons raised to AED 5,000,000 to AED 100,000,000, or the value of the criminal property if greater (Article 27).
Evasion of direct and indirect taxes is a predicate offence.
aml_cft.historical_note: FDL 10/2025 replaces the Federal Decree-Law 20 of 2018 regime; FDL 20/2018 remains relevant only as a historical reference for pre-October-2025 matters.
aml_cft.regulator: Activity-specific supervisory authority; MOET supervises the listed DNFBP sectors in mainland UAE and commercial free zones.
dnfbp_categories: Dealers in precious metals and stones

vara.name: Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority of Dubai
vara.applies_to: Virtual asset service providers operating in Dubai (excluding DIFC)

issuance_rulebook_2026.note: The current VARA Virtual Asset Issuance Rulebook (effective 19 June 2025) sets Category 1 and Category 2 issuance rules, with Annex 1 for fiat-referenced and Annex 2 for asset-referenced virtual assets, and prohibits issuing anonymity-enhanced cryptocurrencies and all related activity. The Exchange Services Rulebook version effective 31 March 2026 adds Exchange Traded Derivative Services Rules (Part V), creating a formal derivatives regime for licensed exchanges. April 2026 issuance guidance interpreting the Issuance Rulebook is reported by secondary press only.

aml_cft.reporting_authority: UAE Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU), through goAML

ubo.name: Ultimate Beneficial Owner
ubo.law: Cabinet Decision 109 of 2023 (Regulation of the Real Beneficiary Procedures)
ubo.previous_law: Cabinet Decision 58 of 2020, superseded with effect from 2023-11-16. Cite it only for conduct predating that date.

penalties.instrument: Cabinet Decision 132 of 2023 (issued 2023-12-15, superseded Cabinet Decision 53 of 2021)
penalties.structure: Graduated per violation: for most violations a written warning for a first breach, up to AED 50,000 for a second and up to AED 100,000 for a third, plus possible licence suspension and closure after a third breach. A liquidator's failure to keep the registers for 5 years is a single AED 100,000 fine.

ubo.summary: In-scope UAE legal persons must maintain and file beneficial-owner information with their registrar. The 25% ownership/voting test is supplemented by control tests; government-owned and financial-free-zone exceptions require separate treatment.
ubo.law_in_force_note: Cabinet Decision 109 of 2023 was issued on 6 November 2023, published in Official Gazette issue 763 and took effect the day after publication. The gazette publication date was not confirmed from a primary source, so the 16 November 2023 in-force date is unverified.

uae_pdpl.name: UAE Personal Data Protection Law
uae_pdpl.executive_regulations_status: No PDPL Executive Regulations found on the UAE Legislation portal or u.ae as of 2026-10-20. Secondary reports conflict on whether they have been issued, so treat their status as unverified.

excise.law: Federal Decree-Law 7 of 2017 (as amended by Federal Decree-Laws 19 of 2022, 7 of 2025 and 17 of 2025)
categories: Liquids used in electronic smoking devices and tools
excise.categories_law: Cabinet Decision 197 of 2025 (in force 2026-01-01, replacing Cabinet Decision 52 of 2019)

rates.goods: Liquids used in electronic smoking devices and tools

rates.rate: AED 0, 0.79 or 1.09 per litre by sugar content (see sweetened_drinks_volumetric)

sweetened_drinks_volumetric.model: Tiered volumetric excise by sugar content, replacing the flat 50% ad valorem rate on sweetened beverages.
sweetened_drinks_volumetric.exempt: Drinks under 5g sugar per 100ml, or sweetened only with artificial sweeteners.
sweetened_drinks_volumetric.certification: A MoIAT Emirates Conformity Certificate is required to evidence sugar content; uncertified drinks default to the high-sugar band (AED 1.09 per litre).

minimum_excise_prices.products: Cigarettes, including conventional and heated cigarettes
Water-pipe tobacco, ready-to-use tobacco, and similar products
Liquids used in electronic smoking devices and tools, whether or not containing nicotine

e_invoicing.name: UAE E-Invoicing
e_invoicing.model: PINT AE on a Decentralized Continuous Transaction Control and Exchange (DCTCE) 5-corner model; e-invoices exchanged via accredited service providers (ASPs) and reported to the FTA through EmaraTax
e_invoicing.penalties_law_note: The MoF eInvoicing programme presentation (October 2026) lists Cabinet Decision 173 of 2026 as the e-invoicing penalties decision and marks Cabinet Decision 106 of 2025 as repealed. The MoF eInvoicing and legislation pages still list Cabinet Decision 106 of 2025, and no text of Cabinet Decision 173 of 2026 had been published as of 2026-10-20. Unverified: confirm with the MoF before quoting penalty amounts.
e_invoicing.status: pilot phase live: the 5-corner model has been operational since July 2026 (pilot launched 2026-07-01 with a selected Taxpayer Working Group; voluntary adoption open to any business). The MoF (27 September 2026, Ras Al Khaimah), the FTA (29 September 2026 joint awareness meeting) and the MoF eInvoicing programme presentation (October 2026) all keep the 30 October 2026 ASP appointment deadline and 1 January 2027 go-live for businesses with revenue at or above AED 50M, and 31 March 2027 and 1 July 2027 for businesses below AED 50M; no extension had been announced as of 20 October 2026. Ministerial Decision 197 of 2026 (in force 1 October 2026, announced 19 October 2026) excludes transactions within a VAT tax group for 24 months from 1 January 2027, removes the UAE data-storage and System Failure notification rules, and sets 14 Business Days to issue and transmit an e-invoice. Businesses must select and contract an ASP, integrate, and then complete the EmaraTax procedures.

changes: Transactions between members of the same VAT tax group are Excluded Transactions for 24 months from 1 January 2027.
E-invoices and e-credit notes must be issued and transmitted within 14 Business Days of the transaction date (previously 14 days).
E-invoice data must be kept for the Tax Procedures Law retention period and produced to the FTA on request; the requirement to store it inside the UAE is removed.
The System Failure definition and the duty to notify the FTA of a System Failure within 2 Business Days (Article 12) are repealed.

Other exclusions are restated: sovereign government transactions, international airline passenger services and ancillary services, airline cargo for 24 months from the system's effective date, and VAT-exempt or zero-rated financial services.

revenue_at_or_above_aed_50m.note: The go-live date is unchanged despite the appointment extension.
revenue_at_or_above_aed_50m.deadline_status: UPCOMING as of 2026-10-20: no extension announced by the MoF or FTA; the MoF eInvoicing programme presentation (October 2026) still shows 30 October 2026.

asp_register.status: The official MoF page (last updated 20 October 2026) lists 69 accredited providers and 3 pre-approved providers under final accreditation assessment (up from 65 and 5 on 13 October 2026). It does not publish a separate overall pre-approved count; that count is unknown, not zero. Final assessment is not full accreditation. The MoF programme presentation (October 2026) reported 10 more providers in the pipeline and about 20 at application review.
asp_register.criteria_note: Ministerial Decision 168 of 2026 (in force 1 October 2026, announced 9 October 2026) repeals Ministerial Decision 64 of 2025 and its amendments, including Ministerial Decision 56 of 2026, and removes the pre-approval stage: providers must complete the accreditation assessment and testing before accreditation. Providers holding preliminary approval under the old framework have up to 30 days from 1 October 2026 to complete the requirements, or the approval is terminated. Providers may still use third-party Peppol Service Provider Products and outsource parts of their service while remaining responsible for compliance. The framework also covers renewal, ongoing evaluation, termination and objections.

technical_docs.format: PINT AE XML (UBL-based) on the 5-corner DCTCE model

e_invoicing.scope_note: applies to B2B and B2G transactions; B2C transactions stay outside the system until a Ministerial decision (Ministerial Decision 244 of 2025, Article 5(2)); phased by revenue band

late_payment_penalty.name: Unified late-payment penalty
late_payment_penalty.basis: 14% per annum on unpaid tax, charged monthly at 14% divided by 12 for every month or part of a month, unifying the late-payment penalty across VAT, Excise and Corporate Tax (replacing the previous escalating monthly model)
late_payment_penalty.note: The calculator rounds any part month up to a whole charged month; confirm the exact calendar-month count with the FTA.

last_refresh_scope: Full review of 2026-10-20: re-verified every field against FTA and MoF primary texts (legislation registers, guides pages and decision PDFs), the Annexure to Cabinet Decision 142 of 2024, the FIU and MoJ AML texts, MOET UBO decisions, VARA rulebooks and u.ae. Changes: Ministerial Decision 197 of 2026 added (e-invoicing tax-group exclusion for 24 months from 1 January 2027, 14 Business Days to issue, UAE storage and System Failure rules removed); MoF ASP register 65 to 69 accredited and 5 to 3 in final assessment; government entities' 31 March 2027 ASP deadline added (MD 244 of 2025); first DMTT Top-up Tax return date of 30 June 2027 confirmed by Article 8.1 of the Cabinet Decision 142 Annexure; DMTT revenue test, Ministerial Decision 96 of 2026 and FTA Decision 6 of 2026 (QFZP distribution AUP report) added; excise goods list corrected to the five categories of Cabinet Decision 197 of 2025 with rates; Article 54 bis input-tax denial corrected to knew or should have known; VAT credit 5-year lapse and the 31 December 2026 refund transition clarified; transfer pricing thresholds sourced to the FTA returns guide and Ministerial Decision 97 of 2023; registration waiver sourced; VARA note corrected (Issuance Rulebook effective 19 June 2025, derivatives in the Exchange Services Rulebook from 31 March 2026); UBO penalty detail and AML fine wording refined; dead Cabinet Decision 137 PDF and non-loading DLA Piper and Deloitte links replaced with MoF and FTA texts. Checked with no change: Corporate Tax rate and band, QFZP de minimis, Small Business Relief to 2029, the 30 November 2026 DMTT registration deadline, FTA Decisions 12, 13, 15 and 17 of 2026, Cabinet Decisions 1, 137 and 149 of 2026, VAT thresholds and directives, Tax Procedures limitation periods, the 14% late-payment penalty, ESR, sweetened-drinks tiers and the 30 October 2026 ASP deadline (no extension); no FTA legislation after 28 September or FTA news after 8 October 2026. Still unverified: Cabinet Decision 173 of 2026 on e-invoicing penalties (named only in an MoF presentation), the VAT cash-payment threshold (no Ministerial decision published), PDPL executive regulations, and the first-year Pillar Two Information Return date.
